description: Crystal Lake Dam lake-rise model. Parameters from the Hydrologic Reference (June 2026): Dinicola 1990 Till Forest HSPF set + 2007 HEC-HMS geometry. US customary units throughout (inches, cfs, acres, acre-feet, feet, hours).

hspf.groundwater_comment: Active-groundwater (baseflow) limb, Till Forest. AGWRC_per_day=0.996 is the Ecology WWHM Appendix III-B calibrated Till value (also outwash/saturated): a daily recession ratio giving baseflow half-life ~173 d (hourly = 0.996**(1/24) = 0.999833) - three orders of magnitude slower than the IRC=0.5/day interflow (~1-day half-life). That separation is what lets the lake hold/rise for days on little rain. KVARY_per_in=0.0 starts the store LINEAR; Ecology's Till value is 0.5/in (faster recession when GW storage is high) - enable and confirm against wet- vs dry-season recession slopes (brief D.5). DEEPFR=0.05 is the fraction of percolation permanently lost out of basin (the ONLY true sink); the brief recommends the low end for a low-relief closed till basin discharging to the lake (Wolock-grid BFI=0.67 argues a strongly GW-supported basin). EPA Tech Note 6 ranges: AGWRC 0.85-0.999, KVARY 0.0-5.0, DEEPFR 0.0-0.50.

watershed.gw_perc_comment: Fraction of bucket overflow that percolates to the active-groundwater limb (the remaining 0.89 becomes fast interflow). This is NOT a loss: of what percolates, only hspf.DEEPFR (0.05) leaves the basin permanently; the other ~95% returns to the lake as slow baseflow (AGWRC). Previously named deep_loss_fraction and discarded entirely - that deleted the whole active-groundwater limb (brief, bottom-line #1). Value 0.11 was calibrated so the Step 6 saturated anchor peaks ~343.1 ft; the short-horizon anchor is unaffected by re-plumbing the slow limb (173-day half-life returns negligibly within 72 h). CALIBRATION FOLLOW-UP: tune gw_perc_fraction + DEEPFR so the model's long-term baseflow share approaches the Wolock BFI=0.67 once clean gauge recessions exist (brief C/D.1). The slow IRC interflow routing also attenuates instantaneous peak inflow (~285 vs HEC-HMS 884 cfs) even though peak elevation matches via volume.

datum.comment: Maps the HA lake-depth sensor reading to absolute elevation: abs = reading + sensor_to_absolute_offset_ft. PROVISIONAL (open item #2): the doc's +339.0 is the staff/WQ frame, but sensor.crystal_lake_depth has a DIFFERENT zero. 338.375 is cross-checked from the existing HA helper crystal_lake_threshold_summer_normal=1.3 (depth) corresponding to the doc's 3-log summer pool 339.675 ft (i.e. 339.675-1.3). Independently corroborated: a hindcast from the June seasonal default lands at ~339.68 ft for the current 1.36 reading. CONFIRM with a field tape-down before trusting absolute thresholds.

primary.comment: soffit_elev_ft (opening top) INFERRED from the rated 110 cfs @ 342 ft taken as the full-flow point: ~3.2 ft above the 338.8 ft sill, 'somewhat taller' than the aux. Above it the opening drowns and flow follows a submerged-orifice (sqrt-head) law. ESTIMATE pending a field measurement of the primary opening. seam_bottom_elev_ft = bare sill 338.8: seams leak from here up to the active stop-log crest.

auxiliary.comment: soffit_elev_ft = bridge underside, measured 2.5 ft above the zero-stop-log datum (338.8 ft) -> 341.3 ft absolute; the flow opening is ~1.3 ft above the 340.0 ft crest. Drowns ~0.9 ft below the 342.2 ft dam crest, so the aux is orifice-limited (flow nearly plateaus) before the dam overtops. seam_bottom_elev_ft = 338.8: the aux stop-log stack runs 338.8 -> 340.0 (same base as the primary, per the 2.5 ft height measured from that datum), so its 7.5 ft of seam leaks whenever the lake is above 338.8.

overtopping.comment: Once the lake exceeds the dam crest (342.2 ft, =thresholds.dam_crest) the whole ~60 ft crest spills as one broad-crested weir, Q = 2.6 * 60 * (h-342.2)**1.5, added on top of the two spillway legs. weir_coeff 2.6 is a standard broad-crested coefficient (US customary); tune once a real overtopping event or a survey of the crest profile is available. This relief caps the modeled rise above the crest: the Step 6 saturated anchor peaks ~0.2 ft lower than the spillway-only model (still within the 343.1 +/-0.5 ft target).

leakage.comment: Seepage through the stop-log seams of EVERY leg, continuously: per leg = cfs_per_ft2 * crest_length_ft * submerged_seam_height, where submerged_seam_height = min(lake, crest) - seam_bottom (capped at the full stack). Present at the bare-board dry recession AND underneath water spilling over the top. cfs_per_ft2=0.0557 is calibrated so the combined primary (10 ft) + aux (7.5 ft) seam leakage at the summer dry equilibrium is ~0.8 cfs, holding the 72 h recession anchor in the observed 339.6-339.8 ft band. cfs_low/high (Reference 4.4a) bound the realized leakage. First-order (linear in submerged height, shared coefficient across legs); needs a real dry spell to calibrate the split and the head dependence.

seasonal_sm_default_frac_of_lzsn.comment: Fraction of LZSN to seed SM by month when insufficient rainfall history exists for replay (Reference 1.5). Dry late-summer -> near 0; near-saturated Dec-Apr -> ~1.0.

uncertainty.comment: Lead-time-dependent multiplicative (log-normal) precip error. median = forecast; low/high are the ~10th/90th pct of (actual/forecast) -- the 80% interval -- and are ASYMMETRIC (fatter high tail: heavy events are biased low, the dangerous direction for EAP thresholds). Grounded in WPC QPF threat-score decay and global precip-overlap skill (see docs/forecast-uncertainty.md). Cool-season PNW frontal/AR regime is the favorable baseline; summer convection widens the band and lowers confidence via season_spread_factor. PLACEHOLDER until site forecast-vs-gauge pairs are logged and fit (spec 3.5).
